hardware_answers.question: Do the wiki's Python install lines work as written on Debian 13? Is python3-serial from apt enough for 'from esp32c5_kismet import board'? What is the minimum Python version for the helper?

answers.answer:
The Remote-Capture install lines work as written on this Debian 13 / Raspberry Pi OS. python3-venv was already installed, so the sudo line was skipped. apt's python3-serial is enough for 'from esp32c5_kismet import board' but not for the helper, which also needs msgpack.

The requirements need Python 3.10 or newer, because websocket-client 1.9.1+ needs it. The helper itself also runs on 3.9 with websocket-client 1.8.0.
answers.evidence:
p16: 'python3 -m venv .venv' exit 0. '.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt' installed msgpack-1.2.3, pyserial-3.5 and websocket-client-1.9.2 on Python 3.13.5. --list worked, and a 30 s capture reached running=1 with 12 BTLE devices; exit 0.

/usr/bin/python3 with python3-serial 3.5-2 imports board. 'from esp32c5_kismet import remote' fails with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'msgpack'" (python3-msgpack is not installed).

p17 (uv interpreters, no sudo):
- 3.9.25: 'Because the current Python version (3.9.25) does not satisfy Python>=3.10 and websocket-client>=1.9.1 depends on Python>=3.10 ... unsatisfiable'. With websocket-client 1.8.0 both test files are ALL OK and a capture runs.
- 3.10.21, 3.11.16, 3.12.14: requirements install, both test files ALL OK, capture runs.

All temporary interpreters were deleted.

hardware_answers.question: Re-measure start and radio-switch times with the current helpers (with the 0.8 s MODE settle): a local source with the board already on the radio versus after a switch; Kismet start to first packets; one remote C helper hopping for 60 s (device counts).

answers.answer: Partial, C local. Launched->capturing is 1.05-1.50 s for the same radio and about 1.5 s for Wi-Fi<->802.15.4, BLE->Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi->BTLE, with 0.8 s of that the MODE settle. It is 2.5 s when the board USB re-enumerates, and in one case (n1) the BTLE switch failed entirely. Kismet start -> first Wi-Fi packet with two Wi-Fi boards: 2.20/2.20, 2.79/3.29 and 2.24/3.66 s. The Python helper took about 1 s from 'opened' to 'capturing'. The 60 s C-remote device count was not run.
answers.evidence: n1, n1b, n1c, g1a-c, g4 logs; rt-py-*.out.

answers.answer: Python helper radio switch, board 10:BD:A3:C8:7D:54 (the board whose Wi-Fi to BLE switch hung once under the C helper). All 25 switches succeeded. Opened to capturing, median: same radio 0.97 s, Wi-Fi to zigbee 1.23 s, zigbee to Wi-Fi 1.36 s, Wi-Fi to BTLE 1.23 s, BTLE to Wi-Fi 1.31 s. MODE to START gap: 0.80 s.
answers.evidence:
p12.out, min/median/max:
- wifi->wifi: start->capturing 1.07/1.23/1.52, opened->capturing 0.81/0.97/1.26.
- wifi->zigbee: 1.49/1.50/1.60, opened 1.23/1.23/1.34.
- zigbee->wifi: 1.62/1.62/1.68, opened 1.36/1.36/1.38.
- wifi->btle: 1.48/1.50/1.59, opened 1.21/1.23/1.34.
- btle->wifi: 1.54/1.57/1.61, opened 1.28/1.31/1.35.
No re-enumeration: 4 by-id links throughout.

The helper always sends MODE first, so even the same radio waits the 0.8 s settle. strace MODE->START: 0.803 s (p3) and 0.803 s (p8).

hardware_answers.question: Do the short source forms esp32c5-ttyACMn, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACMn and esp32c5btle-ttyACMn work on real boards with the current C helper (and the same names with the Python remote helper)?

answers.answer: Yes for the C helper, local and --connect. esp32c5-ttyACM0, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 and esp32c5btle-ttyACM2, run one at a time, each gave 'capturing (wifi|zigbee|btle)' 1.50 s after launch. All four together (two Wi-Fi, zigbee, btle) ran with dlt 127/230/256 and hop lists 42 (1..177) / 16 (11-26) / 1 (37). C --connect worked with esp32c5-ttyACM1 and esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2. The Python remote helper worked with esp32c5-ttyACM1, esp32c5btle-ttyACM3 and esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 (the last with channel options). Python zigbee without options was not run separately.
answers.evidence: g1a/g1b/g1c logs ('esp32c5-ttyACM0 capturing (wifi)' 1.988 s, 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 capturing (zigbee)' 1.965 s, 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' 1.972 s). n1c/g4 src.json. n8t, n9 ('esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 - esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 capturing (zigbee)', 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM3 - /dev/ttyACM3 capturing'), n4r.

answers.answer: This adds to the first agent's run. The BTLE short forms worked on real boards: C local '-c esp32c5btle-ttyACM0' and '-c esp32c5btle-ttyACM2', and '--source esp32c5btle-ttyACM2' through both the C remote and the Python remote helper. So did 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2:channel=20,channel_hop=false' and 'esp32c5-ttyACM2', through all three setups. Log lines: 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM0 capturing (btle)' (local), 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' (C remote), 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - /dev/ttyACM2 capturing' (Python remote).
Yes, the short source forms work with the Python remote helper on real boards: esp32c5-ttyACMn, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACMn and esp32c5btle-ttyACMn, alone or several in one process.
answers.evidence:
All ran with running=1. Link type and hop list per radio:
- esp32c5-ttyACM0: link type 127, 42 channels 1..177.
- esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2: 230, 16 channels 11..26.
- esp32c5btle-ttyACM3: 256, [37].

Python sources on the log lines appear as '<name> - <port> capturing', not '<name> capturing (wifi)'. The C local and C remote sources for the same boards also captured in p2 (b/c).

The four-source run (p10a) and the mix of C local and Python (p10b) also used these names.

hardware_answers.question: Does the wiki's TXTEST script (board.py) run as written on Linux against the current firmware? What are the exact 'Detected new 802.15.4 device' lines and the 802.15.4 rewrap results (channel, frequency, signal)? Does any malformed-TAP message appear?

answers.answer:
The wiki's TXTEST script runs as written on Linux, with the venv python and with /usr/bin/python3 plus apt python3-serial 3.5-2. It exits 0. With a Python remote receiver locked on channel 20, 200/200 frames arrive.

Log lines: 'Detected new 802.15.4 device 00:01' and 'Detected new 802.15.4 device FF:FF'. The devices show channel '20', frequency 2450000 and signal 6 dBm. No malformed-TAP message appeared.
answers.evidence: p3.out. Running TXTEST twice in one Kismet session gives identical frames; the device counts stay at 200 while num_packets reaches 400. The C local receiver is the C run's.

hardware_answers.question: On real boards with both helpers, does channel= set the start channel, and with channel_hop=false keep the source there (802.15.4 on 20, Wi-Fi on a 5 GHz channel, BTLE 37/38/39)? Do 200 TXTEST frames arrive as 200 packets of link type 230?

answers.answer: channel= with channel_hop=false works with all three helpers. zigbee channel=20 gave REST ch '20' hop 0, a single 'CHANNELS 20' with START, and TXTEST 200 -> exactly 200 packets of link type 230; devices 00:01 and FF:FF on channel 20, 2450000 kHz, +9 dBm. Wi-Fi channel=36 gave all 4813 packets at 5180 MHz. channel=36 without hop=false does not start on 36: the hop thread begins during the 0.8 s MODE settle and START went out with 'CHANNELS 13', then it hops. BTLE channel=38 is accepted but shows channel '37', hopping 1, hop_channels ['37','38'], and the helper tunes only 37. channel=200 gives 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1: channel=200 is not a channel the board can tune to in zigbee mode' (typed). Re-adding a board/radio whose closed source record still exists is refused: 'Conflict of new datasource w48lock/E5C50001-...-10BDA3C87D54 and existing datasource w36hop with the same UUID'.
answers.evidence: glock/glock2 logs and strace (168599, 168637, 168648, 169587), glock.pcapng summary, glock2.devs.json, n4r, g3.

answers.answer:
With the Python helper, channel= plus channel_hop=false holds the channel. Zigbee on 20 received 200/200 frames. Wi-Fi on 36 put every frame at 5180 MHz. BTLE channel=38 is accepted but reported as 37.

Without channel_hop=false, channel=36 is not really visited at the start: Kismet's hop list reaches the helper before START, and the first START carried CHANNELS 13.

When a UUID is reused within one Kismet run, the old record's options stay. Going from hopping to locked works. Going from locked to a plain definition stays locked, with both remote helpers.

channel=200 is refused at start-up with exit 2.
answers.evidence:
Zigbee on 20, BTLE on 38 and the startup errors:
- Zigbee on 20: see check 3.
- BTLE channel=38: REST channel '37', hopping 1, hop_channels [37,38]; Kismet appended 38.
- BTLE channel=38,channel_hop=false: channel '37', hopping 0.
- Startup errors: 'python -m esp32c5_kismet.remote: error: esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=200: esp32c5-ttyACM0: channel=200 is not a channel the board can tune to in wifi mode', exit 2. The same form for Wi-Fi 15, zigbee 30 and btle 40.

Wi-Fi channel=36 without channel_hop=false, in a fresh Kismet: REST shows channel 36 and hopping 1. strace shows CHANNELS 1, 5, 9, 13, then 'CHANNELS 13\nDWELL 250\nSTART'.

Reused UUID (p4b), in order:
1. 'lock36' (channel=36,channel_hop=false): locked.
2. Plain 'esp32c5-ttyACM0': definition still 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36,channel_hop=false,name=lock36', hopping 0, 1 CHANNELS write.
3. C remote, plain: the same.
4. ':channel_hop=true': hopping 1.
5. ':name=plain': definition becomes '...channel=36,channel_hop=true,name=plain'.
The OPENREQ carried Kismet's merged definition.

hardware_answers.question: With the sibling's firmware 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, what happens in btle mode (and in zigbee mode on 1.0.0) with both helpers: the 'lost sync (the board sends link type X, not Y)' and 15 s message texts, and the retry cadence? Does Wi-Fi still work?

answers.answer: 1.1.0 (sha256 3453d366...): Wi-Fi 613 packets; Zigbee 200/200. BTLE fails: MODE BLE is silently ignored (no reboot, the stream stays link type 127). The C local helper then logs pairs once every 0.5-1.0 s (34 pairs in 40 s): 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' followed by 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)'. At 15.5 s the helper exits and Kismet shows only 'Data source ... encountered an error: IPC connection closed' and 'Kismet will attempt to re-open the source in 5 seconds. (1 failures)'. It re-opens at +5.1 s, a cycle of about 20 s. The helper's own 15 s text never appears (see problems). The Python helper logs '/dev/ttyACM2 capturing' followed by '/dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)' every 0.9 s. At 15.6 s Kismet shows 'encountered an error: remote connection triggered shutdown: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256))', and it reconnects 5.1 s later. 1.0.0 (sha256 6a9c108f...): zigbee and btle fail the same way ('... not 283' / '... not 256'). The Python zigbee give-up came at 23.1 s in the first cycle, not 15 s. Wi-Fi does NOT work: START is answered with link type 127, but 0 records ever arrive (0 packets in 40 s under Kismet, 0 bytes raw).

Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: The C helper's 15 s give-up message never reaches Kismet: users see only 'IPC connection closed'
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: Seen in 4 of 4 local give-ups (o110.btle.log, o100.btle.log, o100.zigbee.log, earlier n15.log): 0 occurrences of 'no capture from the board', and REST error_reason is 'IPC connection closed'. The helper writes the text as v3 CMD_ERROR (strace in hw2/results/hw2/strace/esp32c5.283245 line 137). Kismet cfe427074's kis_external.cc:1037-1066 dispatch_rx_packet_v3 has no case for KIS_EXTERNAL_V3_CMD_ERROR.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: At capture_esp32c5.c:1383-1388, send the same text as a message before cf_send_error: cf_send_message(caph, errstr, MSGFLAG_ERROR). Kismet logs MESSAGE frames, and the per-source text then appears. Do the same for the cf_send_error at line 925. Until then, change Bluetooth-LE-Capture.md:86, Zigbee-and-Thread-Capture.md:123 and Flashing-the-Firmware.md:335 to say that a local source shows 'IPC connection closed' and is re-opened every ~20 s.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: Kismet counts a repeated TXTEST 200 as duplicates, and kismetdb logs 802.15.4 packets with frequency 0.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: p3 kismetdb: the second batch of 200 identical frames (same seq 0-199) was logged with phyname 'Unknown' and MACs 00:00:00:00:00:00. The device counts stayed at 200 while num_packets reached 400. Every 802.15.4 packet has frequency 0.0, though the devices show 2450000 kHz and signal 6.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Note that device counts rise by 200 only for the first TXTEST in a Kismet session. The frequency=0 in kismetdb comes from the Python helper's signal block, and the C helper was not compared.
